summary.en: Afghan Taliban mortar fire on the northwest Pakistan border killed one civilian and wounded five, and separate Afghan firing near Angoor Adda injured five people. Pakistan responded with strikes on Taliban positions and destroyed border check posts, and launched an operation against illegal Afghans in Peshawar starting Nov 1. The Pakistani minister linked the border closure to a rise in LPG prices. The conflict recorded 1,794 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Afghanske Taliban-mortarild på den nordvestlige Pakistan-grensen drepte en sivil og såret fem, og separat afghansk ildutveksling nær Angoor Adda såret fem personer. Pakistan svarte med angrep på Taliban-posisjoner, ødela grensekontrollposter og igangsatte en operasjon mot ulovlige afghanere i Peshawar fra 1. november. Den pakistanske ministeren knyttet grenselukningen til en økning i LPG-prisene. Konflikten registrerte 1 794 dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Insurgency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
background.extract: Since 2004, an insurgency has been fought in the Pakistani province of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa by Islamist militant groups such as the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), Jundallah, Lashkar-e-Islam (LeI), the Tehreek-e-Nafaz-e-Shariat-e-Mohammadi (TNSM), Al-Qaeda, and their Central Asian allies such as the Islamic State – Khorasan Province (ISKP), Islamic Movement of Uzbekistan, East Turkistan Movement, Jamaat-ul-Ahrar, Ittihad-ul-Mujahideen Pakistan, and elements of organised crime. Before being transformed into an insurgency in 2017, the conflict was a war.
